notes.title: Hades 2 just became 2025's highest-rated PC game, surpassing Expedition 33
notes.notes:
Following up an award-hoarding hit with a sequel is a tough gig - innovations and new content may upset those that worshipped the original, and the expectation bar will always be set sky high. Hades 2 has faced this very challenge, but Supergiant has given it plenty of cooking time in early access to create what appears to be the perfect roguelike sequel. With version 1.0 arriving tomorrow, September 25, critic reviews have just come flooding in. With an average of 94 on Metacritic, Hades 2 is not only being scored more highly than its predecessor, but it has now shot to the top of the aggregator's 2025 chart for PC games, surpassing GOTY frontrunner Clair Obscur Expedition 33.

notes.title: Expedition 33 devs had to "up our game" after Lies of P left studio CEO stunned
notes.notes:
While one is a bruising cousin of Dark Souls, and the other is a strategic, turn-based affair, there's a lot of shared inspiration and visual cues between 2023's excellent Lies of P and this year's GOTY frontrunner, Clair Obscur Expedition 33. Both lean on the Belle Époque era, a period in French history where architecture, art, and technology all rose to an expressive prominence. In a conversation between Lies of P's game director Choi Ji-won, and Sandfall Interactive's CEO Guillaume Broche, the latter admits that the studio had to "up our game" after playing Lies of P, and that the response to the game "validated" what it was trying to achieve with Expedition 33.

notes.title: Clair Obscur Expedition 33 expert beats the game without parries or dodges
notes.notes:
Clair Obscur Expedition 33 is certain to wind up among the year's most memorable games, but the stylish JRPG can also be an immensely tough experience at times. Its slick combat typically requires you to parry, or at least dodge, the hardest-hitting strikes of your foes in order to survive. The good news is that if you take the time to learn all of its encounters, you can beat the entire game without taking a single hit. One particularly enthusiastic soulslike veteran, however, has turned that challenge on its head with a Clair Obscur Expedition 33 'all hit' run, where they tank every single blow with no parries or dodging, and I'm seriously impressed by their ingenuity.

notes.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 (PS5) Review
notes.notes:
It might be on-the-nose to say that a game which is so strongly focused on literal art has reminded me of the potential of video games as an artistic medium, but that’s exactly what Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has done.

The beauty of video games is their potential to bring every aspect of art—visual art, music, drama, writing—to bear through a technological medium, and give players the ability to interact with and control these experiences. And this debut title from France’s Sandfall Interactive excels in all of these departments, providing a feast for the eyes, ears, and soul alongside a stimulating gameplay experience.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is a beautiful hybrid of several genres. At its heart, it is a turn-based RPG following strongly in Persona 5’s footsteps, but featuring prominent action-based prompts—Quick Time Event-like inputs to increase the power of certain attacks, or precise reactions to avoid being attacked in return. notes.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's Andy Serkis says the film industry "could not exist" without games
notes.notes:
Ah, well thank heck for that. I thought I'd spent my weekend hunched over a screen in a goblinesque sweat-trance. No! Says Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 voice actor Andy Serkis: I was simply partaking in some vital culture; a veritable Wildean sophisticate. Film industry folks thought games were "not an art form in any stretch," Serkis told Game Watcher, "and gradually it's taken over the film industry, which could not exist without it." Take that, Roger Ebert's dead wrong dead horse of a dead body.

notes.title: Lorien Testard | Composing the Music of Expedition 33
notes.notes:
[h2]Family Story[/h2]

There are countless soundtracks that I love—each one tied to a different time in my life, carrying memories that have shaped me.

My father worked in a video game shop when I was a baby, and he passed his love for gaming on to me. Many of my childhood memories are deeply connected to video games. I spent hours playing on the Nintendo 64, so the soundtracks of Mario Kart and Mario Party are forever engraved in my heart. As a teenager, I was completely immersed in The Legend of Zelda, a series that left the deepest mark on me. First with Ocarina of Time and Majora’s Mask, then with Wind Waker and Twilight Princess, these games hold some of my most emotional gaming memories, as I shared them with my loved ones.
What I love most about video game music is how it follows us beyond the screen, becoming a companion to our lives, emotions, and both big and small moments. It lingers in our memories, reminding us of who we were when we first heard it and reflecting who we have become when we hear it again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/476753df196adb44648c7a88b67b8f9578067e1c.jpg[/img]

[i]A sample of Lorien’s collection of vintage Videogame magazines and music memorabilia.[/i]

The most unforgettable soundtracks—like The Legend of Zelda—have an incredible ability to breathe life into a world, filling it with unique and deeply moving emotions. The music becomes an organic part of the adventure, shaping the experience as we journey through these universes.
It was this desire to create immersive musical worlds that inspired me to compose my first songs. I dreamed of one day bringing an entire universe to life through music.

[h2]A Life-Changing Collaboration
[/h2]
For a long time, I composed video game music in my free time, writing a new track each week in different styles to refine my skills. At the time, I was a guitar teacher, but once a week, I would compose and upload my work to SoundCloud. After a year, I had about fifty tracks online.

One day, I shared one of my compositions on an indie video game forum. That’s when Guillaume Broche, Game Director at Sandfall Interactive, discovered my work. He reached out and asked if I would compose the soundtrack for his game.

That moment marked the beginning of a beautiful collaboration—one that changed my life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/eaa4a1ea7cb94268b9ee9bf4b48ba2da397e0e09.jpg[/img]

[i]Lorien and Guillaume Broche, Game Director at Sandfall Interactive
[/i]
[h2]Shaping the Musical Identity of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
[/h2]
From the very start, I had a clear vision: to create an immersive musical world where every song tells a story about the game’s universe and its characters. Guillaume shared this vision. We both wanted to craft an extraordinary adventure, filled with discovery and wonder.

Since the project was still in its early stages, I had the incredible opportunity to define its musical identity from the ground up. As I discussed ideas with the team, I received concept art and parts of the script, all of which helped me imagine the sound of Clair Obscur.

Being involved so early meant that the music became an integral part of the game’s essence—a defining element of its identity.

[previewyoutube=urizETxs3_8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Giving Each Character a Voice
[/h2]
I love all musical instruments, and for every scene and every character, I carefully select the ones that best reflect their personalities.

For example, in the themes that have already been released:

[list]
[*] Gustave: The cello in his theme expresses what I feel for his character. I wanted to capture the love he carries for Lumière, despite the ever-present threat of the Paintress.
[*] Monoco: I chose the saxophone as the lead melodic instrument to reflect the madness, energy, and liveliness of the Gestrals.
[/list]

And then there’s one instrument with special significance in the game: the human voice, beautifully brought to life by Alice Duport-Percier.

Voice is at the heart of Expedition 33’s music—almost as if it were the voice of the world itself. It plays a unique role in shaping the game’s story and atmosphere, carrying deep emotions and meaning.
I’ve already seen some interpretations of the game’s lyrics, and it’s always fascinating to read how listeners connect with the music in their own way. The lyrics are sometimes clear, sometimes shrouded in mystery, and I’m eager to see how players will interpret them and shape their own experiences through the music.

[previewyoutube=p00EF6_b5pI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]I Loved Every Second
[/h2]
This project has been an incredible journey, spanning years of work and dedication. I’ve had the chance to collaborate with amazing people and friends.

I don’t yet know how the music will resonate with players, but what I do know is that I loved every second of creating it. I gave everything—I have no regrets. I poured my heart and soul into it, and I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve created.

The full soundtrack will be released alongside the game on April 24, 2025. It has been a part of my life for so long, and it’s hard to express how much it means to finally share this music with you.

Thank you from the bottom of my heart—for listening, for embracing the game and its music, for making it part of your own journey. I can’t wait for you to experience it.

Lorien

notes.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 | Release Date Trailer
notes.notes:
Wow. It’s finally here.  

We’re finally able to reveal the release date for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33! 

[previewyoutube=EsElVZ0sLtU;full][/previewyoutube]
 
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 launches April 24, 2025 on Steam, and pre-orders are now live.  

Dive into our Belle Époque-inspired world filled with surreal enemies, breathtaking landscapes, and unforgettable characters.  

Meet Monoco (voiced by Rich Keeble), the friendly, loyal, but incredibly bloodthirsty Gestral! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/cf871433b14cac06b62938f7cfadaac3670b35a9.png[/img]

Gestrals are friendly beings who enjoy the thrill of battle and view competition as a form of meditation. As one of the few Gestrals who speak the human language, Monoco has adopted quite the scholarly demeanour in spite of his bloodthirsty spirit.  

Though Gestrals are untouched by the Paintress, the prospect of combat entices Monoco to join the Expedition. After defeating an enemy, he can transform into them (using their feet - he has quite a collection!) and unleash their skills in battle, with unique buffs generated by his Bestial Wheel. 

The trailer also introduces Esquie (voiced by Maxence Cazorla), the mythical and powerful being who is able to soar through the heavens and dive deep beneath the sea. Legends also say… he’s lazy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/5edf289c51cfe57e70286d2f34ca6b95b3d493ec.png[/img]

And the legends may be true. 

Esquie enables you to explore the overworld, brimming with secrets, side quests, and challenges. 

And speaking of overworld... 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/af2936458f9cab04837fa73d7e450c19dedaa131.png[/img]

Our world map lets you explore a variety of locations and uncover secrets as you work toward defeating the Paintress. Alongside  level-based areas like the Ancient Sanctuary and Gestral Village, the overworld is packed with hidden oddities to explore and unique locations. These spots feature tough optional battles and side quests, giving you plenty of chances to test your skills and dive into the game’s deep character-building mechanics. 

You’ll also be able to set up camp on the overworld, where you can upgrade weapons and tweak builds, enjoy the game’s beautiful original score on an in-game record player, and chat with your teammates to learn more about their stories and motivations.  

We are excited [b]beyond words[/b] to bring you Expedition 33, and we’ve truly poured all our hearts and souls into creating something we consider truly special.  

Thank you all for your support, and we’ll see you on April 24th.  

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1903340/Clair_Obscur_Expedition_33/]Pre-order the Standard and Digital Deluxe Edition now! [/url]

Tomorrow comes,  

The Expedition 33 Team

notes.title: Meet our English Voice Cast
notes.notes:
Once a year, the Paintress awakens and paints her cursed number on the monolith. 

And everyone of that age turns to smoke, fading into nothing. 

With each passing year, the number falls. More are erased. Soon, she will wake and paint “33.” And we will embark on our final mission—to destroy the Paintress and end her cycle of death, forever. 

We are Expedition 33. 

[previewyoutube=ykQuuDwKRpo;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Meet the English Voice Cast 
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/a64e9838215268dce00bfa17241a2a3f1c8dd566.jpg[/img]

Gustave (voiced by Charlie Cox, Daredevil: Born Again) is a resourceful engineer. Growing up under the Paintress’ shadow in Lumière, he has devoted his life to safeguarding the city. With his final year ticking away, Gustave is ready to risk it all—fighting to defeat the Paintress and reclaim a future for Lumière's children. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/a5df954b6d10b2bec9310f9bc2e9b093a0dc5abc.jpg[/img]

Maelle (voiced by Jennifer English, Baldurs Gate 3) is a shy loner, eager to fly. Orphaned as a child, she has always felt like an outsider in Lumière. Her only connection is with Gustave, her foster brother. Now, at 16—the youngest of the Expedition—Maelle sees this as her chance to escape Lumière and explore the world beyond. 

[quote]“She’s the epitome of a dream character for me - captivating, intricately layered, exquisitely written.” - Jennifer English on Maelle[/quote] 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/2965d4f4764911b2339e0f59c366ce9cd1b1b93e.jpg[/img]

Lune (voiced by Kirsty Rider, Sandman) is a brilliant scholar and mage. The daughter of renowned researchers, she has sacrificed everything to continue their work. Her one goal is to unravel the mystery of the Paintress. She cannot, and will not, allow the Expedition to fail. 

[quote]“Lune has a real drive to her, and she’s clear about her purpose, which was instilled by her parents from a young age. She’s got this power that radiates from her, but she has vulnerabilities too. I also like her witty put downs, and how she knows how to put the men in their place.” - Kirsty Rider on Lune [/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/105278164b1644a1fd262978836c6f770a2a48db.jpg[/img]

Sciel (voiced by Shala Nyx, The Old Guard) is a calm, cheerful warrior. Once a farmer and now a teacher, Sciel embraces every day with joy, masking the pain of a tragic past. She accepts the cruelty of their world, yet her smile hides unspoken scars. While failure doesn't faze her, she remains fiercely committed to the Expedition's success. 

[quote]“I was particularly drawn to Sciel’s wisdom, sense of play, wonder and gratitude, her ability to have this light and playful side despite her deeply melancholic past. I really appreciated her resourceful and philosophical nature, how she remains open to new ways of thinking and how she can use that tool of creativity to help herself and others around her.” - Shala Nyx on Sciel [/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/dce80cd0829c2f90cec17aa6b114319e4b684520.jpg[/img]

Renoir (voiced by Andy Serkis, The Lord of the Rings, Black Panther) is a man driven by ruthless determination. His sole focus is saving his family, but beneath that fierce exterior lies deep, agonizing loss. Renoir knows that victory demands sacrifice—and he’s ready to pay any price.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/e6da784b7a615ebc54b9b03c2007feb115bb4330.jpg[/img]

Verso (voiced by Ben Starr, Final Fantasy XVI) is a mysterious, dangerous stranger. His motives are unclear, but he’s tracking the Expedition’s every move. 

[quote]“The moral ambiguity of Verso was so immediately enticing. He’s such a darkly mysterious character. As an actor, it was so appealing to be able to explore his subtle yet simmering dramatic inner life with the amount of freedom that the Sandfall team gave me.” - Ben Starr on Verso [/quote]

We aren’t done unveiling characters to you yet - Rich Keeble voices a (in his own words) “Loyal, eloquent, terrifying” character that you will meet in good time… 😊. Devora Wilde and Tracy Wiles (also Baldur's Gate 3 alumni) also voice some fantastic characters – so stay tuned!  

[h1] Spring 2025 
[/h1]
We’re a small team from Montpellier, and to be able to work with such talent has been an indescribable honor. We’ve lived and breathed these characters for the past few years, so it was surreal to witness them be brought to life by our incredible voice cast. 

To have the response that we’ve had on this game so far feels like a dream to us. 

Join Gustave, Maelle, Sciel, Lune, and the rest of the Expedition as they embark on a desperate quest to end the Paintress’ reign of death. Follow the trail of past Expeditions and discover their fates. Enter a fantasy world inspired by Belle Époque France, where surreal enemies and breathtaking landscapes await you.

If you love turn-based RPGs but also crave a little real-time action, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is shaping up to be perfect for you. The surrealist adventure takes active combat prompts to their logical extreme, and in doing so opens up the potential for you to tackle its threats at levels far beyond what might ordinarily be possible - if you're good enough. notes.title: Your first look at gameplay from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.
notes.notes:
[i]Once a year, the Paintress awakens and marks her cursed number upon a monolith. Everyone of that age turns to smoke and fades away, erased for eternity. With each passing year, the number ticks down, and a brave group sets out to stop her. [/i]

Expedition 33 is a turn-based RPG with real-time mechanics, centered around the eponymous Expedition as they strive to prevent The Paintress from ever painting again. This preview offers a glimpse into an early area of the game, shortly after the Expedition sets out, focusing on a region known as Flying Waters. Here, Gustave and Lune are searching for Maelle, another member of the Expedition, and must navigate the area to uncover clues to her whereabouts.

[previewyoutube=55rUagD9sVQ;full][/previewyoutube]

We've infused Expedition 33 with rich environmental storytelling. Throughout the game, you’ll encounter numerous destroyed structures, worn paths, and remnants of the Expeditions that came before. For example in Flying Waters, Expedition 68 met their end, and by exploring the setting you can see how they met their demise. 

You can switch the party leader at any time when you traverse the world of Expedition 33, letting them lead the Expedition as you explore the world and overcome the challenges ahead. Whether you prefer to lead with your favorite character or the one best suited for the upcoming battle, the choice is yours. You can also customize their appearance, with unique outfits and hairstyles discoverable across the world. These customized looks have no effect on your character’s skills or abilities, so you are free to use whatever fits your style the best.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/c5984018c5f274d04ac2c2afe0ce1ff45a1c7983.png[/img]

You can interact with the environment using climbing hooks, ledges left by previous Expeditions, or the Grapple in your kit to ascend great heights. Exploration is heavily rewarded throughout the game, and you’ll come across environmental puzzles called Paint Cages that can aid your journey, along with items called Pictos that teach you new abilities. Pictos work similarly to accessories or gear in traditional RPGs, and bestow stat bonuses to the character who has them equipped. They also have unique passive skills associated with them, called Lumina. Having a Picto equipped allows the character to learn the associated Lumina permanently, and you can equip a wide range of them to diversify your builds, and customize your party to suit a preferred playstyle.

[h3]Combat[/h3]

Our battle system is what we call Reactive Turn Based, where you’ll need to input commands when you attack, but also remain reactive whilst enemies attack to effectively defend your party from damage. Players take turns attacking or defending, with the turn order displayed on the left side of the screen. While basic attacks deal low damage, skills often involve a timed reactive command to maximize their effectiveness and add additional bonuses. Skills cost Action Points (AP) to use, and the cost varies between skills. Though you gain one AP per turn, you can customize your build to get AP from other sources - such as successful parries. Some multi-hit skills may allow you to chain an attack combo, unless you fail your inputs. Some may even backfire and cause damage to you if you fail your input, so careful timing and practice will be key to maximizing your effectiveness in battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/3bc1a9e3356181b3ee78ac0e62c5bc7bd696d469.png[/img]

Similarly, when an enemy attacks, you'll need to time your inputs to minimize damage. The timing windows for these inputs vary—dodging has a larger window, allowing you to evade the attack entirely, while parrying has a tighter window that negates damage and can trigger a powerful counter attack if you successfully parry the entire enemy combo. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/a9a8a0c7f82d366961127bee56c823d04908dfbf.png[/img]

[h3]Bosses[/h3]

Bosses may also have unique mechanics or additional challenges to overcome. For example, Goblu is surrounded by flowers in the encounter, which can bestow it with powerful buffs and advantages that can quickly overwhelm the party. In this case, you can make use of the free-aim system to fire at these flowers and close their buds, limiting their effectiveness and ensuring the Expedition has the upper-hand against these powerful adversaries. Finding and exploiting these unique mechanics can be integral to boss battles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/097400e7264a8a4b0468f99bf200d561df5a0483.png[/img]

We hope you've enjoyed this early look at the game, and we're looking forward to sharing more with you soon. We're a young, ambitious team, eager to pay homage to our favorite games in the genre while crafting something unique and entirely our own.

See you soon, Expeditioners!

~ The Expedition 33 Team

notes.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 launches in 2025! We can’t wait.
notes.notes:
[h1]Welcome, Expeditioners![/h1]

Today at the Xbox Games Showcase, we unveiled the launch trailer for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, our reactive turn-based RPG coming to Xbox, PS5, and PC next year. 

[previewyoutube=o9KQ4rlymEQ;full][/previewyoutube]

The city of Lumière is shrouded in a grim ritual. Once a year, the Paintress marks an age on her monolith, sealing the fate of those who reach it. Soon, she will paint 33, condemning all of that age to death. With only one year left to live, the members of Expedition 33 set out to destroy the Paintress and end this cycle forever.

[h2]Meet some of the Expeditioners.[/h2]

[h3]Gustave[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/c0152e114fd2493ac879d3c87091430d267cb53a.jpg[/img]

You’ll play as Gustave, a diligent engineer who hopes to change the future for his apprentices and all of the children of Lumière. You will lead the Expeditioners through diverse and breathtaking realms, and forge deep bonds with your companions along the way. Unravel their stories, and piece together the mystery of the Paintress’ power.

[h3]MAELLE[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/d9e97fd1db98f651ef40a5269ae83bda3a3ebe18.jpg[/img]

Maelle is one of your early companions and Gustave’s foster sister. As an orphan from infancy, she finds it difficult to trust others and has never felt at home in the city of Lumière. The expedition is a way for her to escape the confines of the city, and though she does not care much about the Paintress, her longing to be free is powerful motivation.

We’ll be revealing more characters over the next few months. We can’t wait to share them and their stories with you all! 

[h3]Reactive Turn-Based Battle System[/h3]

We’re huge fans of turn-based RPGs, action games, and Souls-likes. We wanted to create something that blends the strategic depth of turn-based combat with the thrill of real-time actions - which resulted in our unique reactive turn-based system. Master the defense systems—dodge, parry, and counterattack in real-time—to turn the tide of battle in your favour.

[h3]Join Us on This Journey[/h3]

We’re Sandfall Interactive, a small team located in Montpellier, France. We’ve poured our hearts into creating this game and invite you to discover the depths of its stories and battles in 2025. We’ll be regularly updating our Steam, [url=expedition33.com]Website[/url], and Social Media with more information about the game, characters, and development updates as time goes on. You can join the Expedition on our [url=expedition33.com]website[/url] and unlock exclusive subscriber rewards, and get the latest updates straight to your inbox.

[url=https://www.expedition33.com/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45053496/41d0767c529546302a5968c7f72b22ce01b51690.png[/img]
